chunks.title: About Afaq
chunks.text:
I'm Afaq Ahmed, a data engineer in Espoo, Finland with about five years of project experience. The work starts with a decision someone has to make on Monday: which operational trend matters, which sprint is slipping, which product is actually selling.

Then the data has to get boring. One grain, validated loads, a pipeline that can restart. Python, Spark, SQL, dbt, or Fabric — whichever already fits the stack. The report only ships after that.

chunks.title: Student data platform
chunks.text:
Student data platform (Pipelines & analytics)
Context: University of Eastern Finland
Pipelines, a dimensional warehouse, and Power BI for enrollment, performance, and feedback.
Problem: Academic reporting depended on manual work across enrollment, grades, and feedback. Staff waited hours for a report, and odd records — a sudden GPA jump, a missing enrollment id — took too long to find.
Approach: Built ETL and ELT jobs in Python, PySpark, and SQL over more than 5 million records. Modeled student, faculty, and course data in a warehouse, published Power BI for retention, graduation, dropout risk, and workload, and added Python checks plus checkpointing so Spark jobs could restart without corrupting a load.
Outcome: Manual processing time fell by 60%. Warehouse queries ran about 45% faster, and report generation moved from hours to minutes. Dashboards made the figures easier for academic staff to reach, and anomaly checks cut investigation time by about 40%.
Stack: Python, PySpark, SQL, Power BI
Tags: Python, PySpark, SQL, Power BI
Metrics: 60% less manual processing; 45% faster warehouse queries; 40% faster anomaly checks

chunks.title: Engineering delivery analytics
chunks.text:
Engineering delivery analytics (dbt & Azure DevOps)
Context: GagaMuller · Dublin
A pipeline and live Power BI so leads could see backlog, sprint risk, and capacity without a manual export.
Problem: Sprint planning sat on exported boards. Engineering leads and managers could not see backlog health, project risk, or resource load in one place.
Approach: Pulled Azure DevOps APIs into an end-to-end pipeline with Python and dbt, then built Power BI that stayed current for leads and senior managers. A second view covered construction projects: risk, resources, and procurement on the same reporting habit.
Outcome: Backlog analysis time dropped by about 75%. Sprint planning accuracy improved by about 25% across Scrum teams. On the construction work, delivery moved about 25% faster and resource use improved by about 30%.
Stack: Python, dbt, Azure DevOps, Power BI
Tags: Python, dbt, Azure DevOps, Power BI
Metrics: 75% less time on backlog analysis; 25% better sprint planning accuracy; 30% better resource use

chunks.title: WayLoader on Microsoft Fabric
chunks.text:
WayLoader on Microsoft Fabric (Lakehouse)
Context: GagaMuller · WayLoader
A lakehouse and pipelines so product sales reporting was no longer a manual refresh.
Problem: Sales and product reporting lagged the business. People assembled numbers by hand, so a decision often waited on a stale extract.
Approach: Stood up Data Factory, a lakehouse, and pipelines in Microsoft Fabric, and shaped the data so Power BI could show product sales without a fresh spreadsheet each time.
Outcome: Data was about 70% fresher. Manual reporting time fell by about 50%, and product sales were visible to the people who needed them.
Stack: Microsoft Fabric, Data Factory, Lakehouse, Power BI
Tags: Microsoft Fabric, Data Factory, Power BI
Metrics: 70% fresher product data; 50% less manual reporting

chunks.title: Early diabetes detection
chunks.text:
Early diabetes detection (Applied research)
Context: Master’s thesis · University of Eastern Finland
A hybrid deep learning model aimed at catching diabetes earlier, next to the production analytics work.
Problem: Earlier detection needs a model shaped around the signals in the data, not a single architecture chosen by habit.
Approach: Researched and built a hybrid deep learning model for early diabetes detection as the master’s thesis, grounded in coursework on machine learning, deep learning, applied image processing, and natural language processing.
Outcome: A research model focused on earlier detection, kept separate from the warehouse and dashboard work so each has a clear job.
Stack: Python, Deep learning, Machine learning
Tags: Deep learning, Python, Research

chunks.title: What kind of work do you take on?
chunks.text:
Q: What kind of work do you take on?
A: Pipelines, warehouses, BI, and applied machine learning when the decision needs a model. Education, construction, retail, and product analytics are the domains I have shipped in.

chunks.title: Can you own both the pipeline and the report?
chunks.text:
Q: Can you own both the pipeline and the report?
A: Yes. The usual delivery is ingestion, a tested model, and Power BI or Tableau with one definition per metric.

chunks.title: Is this only batch analytics?
chunks.text:
Q: Is this only batch analytics?
A: Most of the work is batch and warehouse-centric. I also pull APIs such as Azure DevOps, orchestrate with Airflow, and design for fresher data when the business is waiting on yesterday’s extract.

chunks.title: What do you work with?
chunks.text:
Q: What do you work with?
A: Python, PySpark, SQL, ETL/ELT, dbt, dimensional modeling, data quality, Microsoft Fabric, Databricks, Azure Data Factory, Spark, Airflow, medallion architecture, Power BI, Tableau, BigQuery (basic), Git, Azure DevOps, CI/CD, Docker, and Agile delivery.

Q: Are you available?
A: Open to roles and project work from Finland and remote, EU-friendly hours. Send a short brief through the form or email.
